a-new-town.title: In a new town
a-new-town.summary: Someone moves to a small seaside town for work, feels lonely, and finds a way in through the library. Places, feelings and making friends.
translation: Last month I moved from Osaka to a small town for work. It is an old apartment fifteen minutes' walk from the station. The room is not big, but I can see the sea from the window.
The first week, I did not know a single person, and I was a little lonely. When I got home from the office, I cooked alone every evening and ate alone.

One Sunday morning, I tried going to the library nearby. In front of the library was a small park, where children were running with a dog. Inside, there were lots of books on the town's history and old photos.
While I was looking at the photos, a woman next to me spoke to me: "Is this your first time in this town?" Her name was Ms. Mori, and she runs a flower shop near the station.

Ms. Mori told me about all sorts of places in town: a fish shop that is cheap and good, a café that stays open late at night, a hill where you can see the fireworks well in summer. I wrote them all on my map.
After that, I began dropping in at Ms. Mori's shop at weekends. Last week I had lunch with her friends at a diner near the sea. Now I am slowly starting to like this town.

cooking-class.title: Cooking class
cooking-class.summary: A poor cook signs up for weekly lessons, learns fish and meat dishes, and plans a birthday dinner. Food, study and hobbies.
translation: I am bad at cooking. About all I can make myself is rolled omelette and curry. So this spring I started going to a cooking class every Saturday.

The class is on the third floor of a building in front of the station. There are eight students, some university students and some office workers. The teacher used to work at a famous hotel, and her explanations are very easy to understand.

The first day was a fish dish. The teacher told us, "Choose fresh fish. Good ones have clear eyes and a shining body." It took me a long time to cut the fish, and I was much slower than the person next to me.
Last month we learned a meat dish. If you simmer beef on a low heat for a long time, it becomes very tender. When I tasted it, it tasted the same as the teacher's, and I was really happy.
After the class is over, we all eat what we made and chat. We talk not only about cooking but also about work and travel. I have made three friends in the class.
Next Sunday is my mother's birthday. I plan to cook every dish I learned in the class for my family. I am a little worried, but I am looking forward to it already.

the-blue-umbrella.title: The blue umbrella
the-blue-umbrella.summary: An umbrella left on a crowded train turns into a day out at the end of the line. Trains, phone calls and a lost-property office.
translation: It happened on a day when heavy rain had been falling since morning. So as not to be late for a meeting, I hurried out of the house. In my hand was the blue umbrella my older sister gave me for my birthday last year.

The train was very crowded. I stood my umbrella near the door and read the meeting documents on my phone. When I reached the station for my office, I got off the train in a hurry. I did not think of the umbrella at all.
When I left the station, it was still raining. Only then did I notice I had no umbrella. The meeting was soon, so I bought a plastic umbrella at a convenience store and ran to the office.

After work, I phoned the station's lost-property centre. The station attendant asked about the umbrella's colour and shape, and the time of the train I took. When I answered, "It's a blue umbrella with a picture of white flowers," I was told, "One moment, please."

After about five minutes, the attendant told me, "We have it. It is at the last station on the line." The last station is an hour away from my home, but I decided to go and pick it up the next Saturday.

On Saturday, I collected my umbrella at the last station. Outside the station it was sunny, and there was a big river nearby. Since I had come all that way, I took a walk along the river and had a coffee in a small café. Thanks to forgetting my umbrella, it turned into a lovely day.

a-letter-to-my-teacher.title: A letter to my teacher
a-letter-to-my-teacher.summary: A student writes to her Japanese teacher from a summer trip by the northern sea. Travel, family and polite letter language.
translation: Dear Mr. Yamamoto, how are you? I hear it is very hot in Tokyo every day. I am using my summer holiday to visit a town by the sea in the north with my family.

This town is much cooler than Tokyo, and in the mornings and evenings it is almost cold. The inn we are staying at is an old building built more than a hundred years ago, and from our room we can see the sea and the sky together.

Yesterday I got up early and went to the market at the port with my younger brother. The market was selling lots of fish I had never seen, and my brother took photos the whole time. For lunch we ate a fish dish at the market's diner. It tasted completely different from the fish we eat in Tokyo.

In the afternoon my father drove us to a small art museum on top of a hill. It collects the paintings of an artist born in this town, and many were bright paintings of the sea and flowers. I stood in front of a painting of the blue sea for a long time.
You said in class, "When you travel, try writing about what you saw in Japanese," so I wrote this letter. I think it still has many mistakes, but I would be glad if you read it.
I look forward to seeing you at school in September. Please take care of yourself, and have a good summer holiday.
10 August, Akiko Kimura

at-the-doctors.title: At the doctor's
at-the-doctors.summary: A fever means a day off work, a long wait and a doctor's instructions. The body, illness and medicine.
translation: Last Wednesday, when I got up, my head hurt badly and my body felt heavy. When I took my temperature, it was as high as 38 degrees. I phoned the office and decided to take the day off.
The clinic near my home opens at nine. Although I arrived a little early, the waiting room was already full of people. At reception I wrote my name and address, and waited about an hour.
The doctor was a kind-looking woman. She said, "Please open your mouth wide," and looked at my throat. Then she listened to my chest.
"It's a cold," the doctor said. "It isn't anything serious, so there's no need to worry." Then she explained, "I'll give you three days of medicine. Take it three times a day, after meals."
She also told me, "No exercise this week; rest at home. Keep your baths short. If your fever doesn't go down, come back again."

When I got home, I took the medicine and slept all day. By the evening of the next day my fever had gone down, and I felt a little better. I like running every morning, but I plan to stop until next week.

my-japanese-exam.title: My Japanese exam
my-japanese-exam.summary: A learner prepares for a first Japanese exam, with a plan for kanji and help from someone who studies the language. Study, tests and questions.
translation: I have been studying Japanese since last year. This year I decided to take a Japanese exam for the first time, in December.
The hardest part is kanji. One kanji can have several readings, and many characters look alike. For example, at first I often mixed up 待つ (to wait) and 持つ (to hold).
So I decided to practise kanji for fifteen minutes on the train every morning. When I learn a new character, I think of three words that use it and write them in my notebook.

Once a week I meet Nakamura-san, who researches Japanese at a university, and ask about things I don't understand. Nakamura-san told me, "If you read while thinking about what each sentence means, you'll learn the kanji faster too."

A week before the exam, I timed myself and tried last year's questions. When I checked the answers, I had 70 points. Thinking that might not be quite enough to pass, I practised the reading questions in particular over and over.

On the day of the exam it had been snowing since the morning, but I left home early, so I reached the venue on time. I don't know the result yet. But I can read more kanji than before, so I'm glad I kept studying.

my-brothers-wedding.title: My brother's wedding
my-brothers-wedding.summary: A family gets ready for a wedding by the sea: choosing clothes, a song from students and a short speech. Family, colours and celebrations.
translation: Last month my older brother got married. His partner is a friend from his university days who now works as an English teacher. The wedding was held at a church with a view of the sea.

A week before the ceremony, I went to a department store with my younger sister to buy clothes. My sister chose a red dress, but our mother told her, "Red will stand out more than the bride, so pick another colour," and she changed to a blue dress. I went with a black Western-style outfit.
On the day of the wedding it was sunny from the morning, and the breeze felt lovely. Our parents had been greeting relatives since early morning and looked very busy.

The people from my brother's company and the bride's students came to the party after the ceremony. The students sang a song in English and handed the couple a bouquet. Cheerful music was playing in the hall, and everyone looked happy.

At the end of the party, my brother gave a short speech. "When I was little, Dad often got angry with me. But now I really understand how he felt. From now on, the two of us will work together and build a cheerful family." Hearing that, my father cried a little.
After I got home, I sent my brother the photos I had taken that day. He replied, "Thanks. It turned into a special day."

rice-fields-in-autumn.title: Rice fields in autumn
rice-fields-in-autumn.summary: A family helps a grandfather bring in the rice harvest after a typhoon. Seasons, nature and the countryside.
translation: My grandfather grows rice in a small village near the mountains. Every year in autumn, the whole family goes to his house to help with the rice harvest.
From the station to my grandfather's house, you walk about thirty minutes along a narrow road. On both sides of the road, golden rice fields spread out, and lots of red dragonflies fly in the sky.
This year a big typhoon came in September, so my grandfather had been worried the whole time. Some of the rice plants were knocked down by the strong wind, but he says most of them were fine.

From morning until evening we all cut the rice. My grandfather uses a machine too, but he cuts the corners of the fields by hand. I'm not used to it, so I stopped to rest many times. In a tree nearby, birds were calling loudly.

In the evening we ate vegetable dishes my grandmother had made, and rice cooked from last year's harvest. My grandfather laughed and said, "The rice you grow yourself is the most delicious in the world."
My grandfather turns eighty this year. He said, "I'll rest my body over the winter, and work hard again from spring." I think I'll come and help again next year too.

borrowing-books.title: Borrowing books
borrowing-books.summary: Getting a library card takes two tries and comes with a list of rules. Rules, forms and everyday errands.
translation: I love reading, but buying books costs money. So I decided to borrow books from the city library nearby.

People borrowing books for the first time have to get a card. The person at the desk asked me, "Do you have something that shows your address?" I showed a letter from my bank, but was told that couldn't be used.
The next day I took my driving licence and went again. When I wrote my name, address and phone number on the form, they made my card straight away.

The person at the desk also explained how borrowing works. You can borrow up to ten books at a time, for two weeks. The newest issues of magazines can't be taken out, so apparently you read them inside the library.

I was also told, "Please be careful about one thing. If you go past the return date, you can't borrow books for the following week. When the library is closed, please put books in the return box beside the entrance."

That day I borrowed a cookbook, a book of photos of old factories, and three novels. When I got home, I tried cooking a dish from the book in the kitchen. From now on I plan to go to the library every week.

my-first-part-time-job.title: My first part-time job
my-first-part-time-job.summary: A student starts work at a bakery at 6 a.m., makes mistakes at the till, and learns why one bread matters so much. Work, people and a small town.
translation: After starting university, I began a part-time job at a bakery near the station. The owner, Mr. Kobayashi, is a man in his fifties who has been making bread for over thirty years.
Work starts at six in the morning. For the first week, my main jobs were cleaning the shop and carrying heavy bags of flour. I wasn't used to physical work, so I was very tired every day.

From the second week, I also started working at the till. At first I got the money wrong and caused customers trouble. Mr. Kobayashi didn't get angry. He told me, "Making mistakes isn't a bad thing. You just need to be careful not to make the same mistake twice."
This shop has a special bread: a sweet cream bun that has been made since Mr. Kobayashi's father's time. When it comes out of the oven at seven every morning, it all sells out in about ten minutes.

One morning, the oven suddenly stopped and wouldn't work. Mr. Kobayashi phoned a repair company right away, but was told the repair person wouldn't come until the afternoon. That day, we put up a sign in front of the shop saying, "No special bread today."

The next morning, even before we opened, more customers than usual were waiting outside. Some said, "We couldn't have it yesterday." I realised that this shop's bread is something special to the people of the town.
